conviction_note: Event confirmed by the company's own Q1 RNS. Q2 numbers are new, but the FY27 guide (adjusted PBT consensus £234.3m, which the company sourced itself) is very likely to be reiterated rather than moved, and every finding I have is a proxy or something already public. So the findings net to about 0. abs_move is 4.5: above the name's 2.0% median because the half's second quarter is unseen and the stock fell 3.4% on the day before the print with no news, but below the 7% European base because this is a low-volatility staple whose 12 observed reactions never exceeded 6.7%. p_up is 54, a faint lean from strong Q1 volume and a lower bar after today's fall. The scaled number (+0.36) and the findings sum (0.0) differ only in noise.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 volume grew 8.2% (LFL +6.4%) with Eye poultry capacity and new houmous and pet listings, so H1 should show continued volume-led growth. But Q1 is already public and the company has already guided FY27 in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims: -3.75% (2024-11-26) and +2.5% (2025-11-25), both with strong volume growth; the stock has both sold and bought the H1 beat
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the Q1 numbers are four months old and the stock has drifted up since. Only Q2 is unseen, and nothing sources it.
findings.independence: Sainsbury's H1 (finding 5) is a separate source pointing the same way

findings.finding: UK pig prices fell sharply y/y through H1: AHDB SPP 177.97p/kg in the week to 11 Jul 2026, 29.74p below a year earlier and over 20p below the five-year average, with slaughter up 7% y/y. That is lower input cost for a primary processor, partly offset by weaker returns in Cranswick's own pig farming and by lower exports.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2019 margin warning (-20%) came on a pig-price spike; falling prices have historically been the benign case, but no recent print has been sized on it
findings.why_not_priced: Public series and the transmission is ambiguous. Cranswick said in Q1 that 'the benefit of lower input prices was passed onto the Group's customers', which argues against a margin windfall. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: AHDB 9 Apr 2026 update shows the same downward drift (https://ahdb.org.uk/news/downward-drift-continues-for-gb-pig-pricing-but-eu-on-the-up-pork-market-update)

findings.finding: On 26 Oct 2026 the UK government launched a consultation (open to 21 Dec 2026) on phasing out high-concentration CO2 stunning of pigs. The release may carry Cranswick's first comment on capex or cost for its pork primary sites, including the £100m Hull expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried a regulatory capex item of this kind; the stock rose from 5,320p on 26 Oct to 5,630p by 16 Nov, so the announcement itself was not sold
findings.why_not_priced: The consultation is public. What is unpriced is any number management attaches to it, and they may attach none. The AHDB pork council chair calls it 'a huge source of potential risk for our levy payers'.

findings.finding: Avian influenza: GB declared an AIPZ from 11 Nov 2026, with commercial-poultry H5N1 cases near Dersingham and Dereham, Norfolk (9 and 12 Nov). This is a risk to the H2 outlook tone for poultry, now about 20% of group revenue and centred on Eye in Suffolk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior HPAI seasons (2025-26 had many Suffolk/Norfolk cases) did not stop the Jan 2026 Q3 upgrade (+2.72%)
findings.why_not_priced: It is seasonal and public, and the company has managed it before. It matters only if the outlook statement adds caution, which is why it is small.

findings.finding: Sainsbury's, a counterparty that reported after Cranswick last spoke, said H1 (28 weeks to 12 Sep 2026) grocery sales rose 2.9% to £13.2bn 'driven by steady volume growth'. That points to a supportive retail volume backdrop through Cranswick's Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured on a retailer read-through
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and only a proxy for Cranswick's own volumes. It adds little beyond the Q1 statement.
findings.independence: Cranswick's own Q1 statement (finding 1) points the same way

baseline_tension: The baseline leans mildly positive (+0.83: modest disclosed short, covering slightly, flat 20d run-up). My findings net to zero, and today's unexplained -3.4% fall (run_up_5d -4.97%) lowers the bar slightly. Nothing I found disputes the lean or beats it.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic-UK half (Investegate's RNS list, AHDB pig-price updates, gov.uk disease and policy notices) was the primary documentary base, but all of it is public and wire-read; the only domestic-only items, the AHDB pork council chair's reaction to the CO2 consultation and the absence of any September trading update in the RNS list, add context, not an unpriced number.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the Q1-momentum finding went from +0.4 to +0.1, since only Q2 is unseen
'Your own caveat has to reach the number': the pig-price finding went from +0.3 to +0.15, because the company itself said lower input prices were passed to customers
'A narrow proxy loses / macro-to-company is a hypothesis': the Sainsbury's read-through went from +0.2 to +0.15 and the CO2 consultation from -0.3 to -0.2 (no company number yet)

'Size the move on what is new; let reaction history move p_up, not abs': abs_move went from 4.0 to 4.5 because the Q2 numbers are unseen. The likely reiterated guide (median 2.3% in the measured set) and the staple's history keep it well below 7%
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' and the unsourced H1 bar: p_up went from 55 to 54
